truekapp.headline: A barter marketplace I built and took all the way to production
truekapp.problem: Users needed to negotiate item swaps instantly, without page refreshes.
truekapp.solution: A complete Laravel platform with real-time private messaging, trade workflows and an admin panel.
truekapp.section_about: A full-stack barter marketplace where people swap items without money — post what you no longer use, propose trades, chat and rate each other. It began as my final degree project and I pushed it far beyond that: a real app running in production on my own server. Built with Laravel 12 and a service-oriented architecture, it brings together real-time messaging, an AI assistant and semantic search, shipped through a CI/CD pipeline with an automated test suite on every push.
truekapp.section_features:
Real-time chat over WebSockets (Laravel Reverb) with authorized private channels
AI assistant with agentic RAG + tool calling (Google Gemini): answers questions, proposes trades and can re-search the catalog mid-conversation
AI photo-to-listing: take a photo and Gemini Vision suggests the title, category and description
AI image moderation that blocks inappropriate uploads before they're stored
Semantic search that ranks the catalog by meaning, reusing embeddings
A "wishlist" with automatic matching, plus favorites
Trade system with proposals, ratings and reputation
REST API with token authentication (Laravel Sanctum)
Fully bilingual (EN/ES) with a permission-based admin panel and a daily-reset public demo
truekapp.section_tech:
Backend: Laravel 12, PHP 8.3, service-oriented architecture
Real-time: Laravel Reverb (WebSockets)
AI: Google Gemini (chat, embeddings + vision) with RAG and function calling
Database: MySQL
Frontend: Blade, Tailwind CSS, Alpine.js, Vite
Auth & API: Laravel Sanctum
Testing: Pest (120+ tests, incl. AI assistant evals) · Code style: Laravel Pint
truekapp.section_deploy:
My own VPS (Hetzner, Ubuntu) configured by hand — no Forge/Ploi panels
Nginx + PHP-FPM + MySQL set up and managed manually
Supervisor keeps the Reverb daemon and the queue worker alive
SSL via Let's Encrypt, with Cloudflare in front (CDN + DDoS/WAF + CSAM scanning)
CI/CD with GitHub Actions: the test suite runs on every push
A daily cron rebuilds the demo, plus a security-hardening pass (CSP, rate limits, headers)

managepoint.headline: Internal management platform with automated reporting
managepoint.problem: Gaming venue operations relied on manual processes and scattered data across multiple systems.
managepoint.solution: Developed a full-stack management system with role-based access control, automated PDF report generation, and optimized database queries via Laravel migrations.
managepoint.section_about: An internal full-stack platform for managing a gaming venue's day-to-day operations and staff. It replaced manual processes and data scattered across several systems with a single, role-aware management tool built on Laravel.
managepoint.section_features:
Admin panel with role-based access control (RBAC) and user management
Automated PDF report generation for business operations, with historical tracking
Centralized operational data that replaced manual, multi-system workflows
Optimized database queries for fast reporting over historical data
managepoint.section_tech:
Backend: Laravel, PHP, service-oriented structure
Database: MySQL with a relational schema designed through Laravel migrations
Frontend: Blade + Tailwind CSS
Performance: query optimization for reporting-heavy views

valorant.headline: Fan-made Valorant data explorer with live player lookup and interactive tools
valorant.problem: I wanted a Valorant tool that combined game data with real player stats, no backend of my own, while respecting third-party API rate limits and Riot's fan project rules.
valorant.solution: React + Vite SPA with agent, weapon, map and bundle browsing, an interactive damage calculator, and a player lookup that aggregates stats from the last 10 games. The main technical challenge was consuming two third-party APIs with no backend, managing rate limits through a shared throttle across routes.
valorant.section_about: A React + Vite SPA that pairs valorant-api.com (game assets, no key) with the Henrik Dev API (live player data, key-protected) in one tactical interface. It's a full rebuild of an early vanilla-JS project, now with an English UI and a custom Valorant-inspired design system.
valorant.section_features:
Player lookup by Riot ID with aggregate stats: K/D/A, headshot %, ACS and win rate
Live Radiant top-10 leaderboard across six regions
Interactive weapon damage calculator and real-world map callout overlays
Bundle ↔ theme cross-reference that surfaces matching skins, sprays and gear
valorant.section_tech:
React 18 + Vite + React Router + Tailwind CSS
Serverless proxy keeps the API key off the client, mirrored in the Vite dev server
Rate limiting in depth: edge caching, per-region cache and a sliding-window throttle
Lazy-loaded routes and module-level caching for fast loads

frakt24.description: Responsible for the design, implementation, and long-term ownership of several core modules in a multi-tenant logistics SaaS. My work spans solution design, backend development, and cross-platform feature delivery — turning business requirements into reliable production features while upholding code quality, testing, and best practices across the team.
frakt24.highlight1: Incrementally modernizing a legacy PHP (mysqli) codebase to Laravel — calling Laravel services from legacy code without disrupting production.
frakt24.highlight2: Integrating third-party hardware APIs (GPS, tachograph) and owning the data contracts that bridge the web backend with the Flutter mobile app via Firebase/Firestore.
frakt24.highlight3: Owning finance-grade modules with strict transactional integrity and multi-tenant data isolation under concurrency — atomic transactions, row-level locking, and idempotent requests.
frakt24.highlight4: Diagnosing non-trivial production bugs through root-cause analysis across the backend, integrations, and data pipelines.

gesa.description: Sole developer responsible for an AI-powered nutrition app end to end — I built both the Laravel backend and the Flutter mobile client, owning architecture, integrations, and delivery across both repositories.
gesa.highlight1: Built the entire Laravel backend — REST API, data modeling, and business logic powering the app.
gesa.highlight2: Developed the full Flutter client and kept strict parity across the backend and mobile repositories.
gesa.highlight3: Owned all integrations, push notifications, AI nutritional analysis (image & PDF recognition), and real-time Firestore sync.
